newsitem.title: USA: Miami port director resigns amid finance questions.
newsitem.headline: Miami port director resigns amid finance questions.

text.p: Port of Miami Director Carmen Lunetta submitted his resignation amid calls for a complete investigation of the books at the deficit-laden facility, the Miami Herald reported.
Lunetta faxed his resignation late Friday night to County Manager Armando Vidal.
"After much thought, deliberation and discussions with my family, I wish to advise you of my decision to retire as director of the Port of Miami, effective July 31, 1997," Lunetta wrote in the fax.
Lunetta, 67, had been director of the seaport for 38 years.

The Herald said his resignation came after Dade County, which runs the port, released boxes of records showing port money had been spent on Super Bowl tickets, luxury car rentals and campaign contributions, including contributions to current county commissioners.

Last week, a seaport report released under pressure from commissioners revealed that the port had a $22 million deficit and that county general funds had been used to offset port losses for several years.
The revelations prompted Commissioner Miriam Alonso and Commissioner Jimmy Morales, who chairs the commission's finance committee, to call for a complete investigation of the seaport's books.
Lunetta's secretary said he was out of town Monday and would not be back until Tuesday. County officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
